subject: ventures/monastery-site
professional: a webmaster or communications officer for a Catholic abbey or convent (with an accessibility reviewer for WCAG and a canon-law-aware development director for the giving page); they would check first that the site builds, the vocation form and giving link work, contrast is legible, and nothing false about gifts is printed

evidence.correctness: Ran the engine and recomputed independently. (1) WCAG contrast for all 8 text pairs in all 6 palettes recomputed in a separate Python implementation of the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula: all 48 values equal site.mjs contrast() to 3 decimals (e.g. benedictine ink/bg 15.397, carmelite accent/bg 6.458, the lowest pair in any palette) and all are >= 4.5. (2) Giving meter: abbey.json campaign raised 152000 of goal 400000 -> 38%; built home page contains 38% and '$152,000 of $400,000 as of 1 October 2026'. (3) With site.url set to https://abbey.example.org the sitemap lists https://abbey.example.org/about.html, robots.txt carries the Sitemap line, give.html has the matching canonical. (4) parseLines on '4:30 | Vigils | public' gives {time:'4:30',name:'Vigils',public:true}. (5) JSON-LD Event on the events page matches the config (startDate 2026-12-05, schema.org attendance mode). Defects found: the sitemap writes relative <loc>./index.html</loc> when site.url is unset (invalid per sitemaps.org; the checklist does flag the missing URL as low), and safeUrl is bypassed by an embedded tab or newline.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim by running it: twelve page types plus 404 (16 files built from examples/abbey.json: index, about, horarium, vocations, visit, events, news, prayer, shop, give, contact, privacy, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, 404.html); six palettes; launch checklist (checkSite) with high/medium/low findings, ran against a hostile giving link and got the high finding; CLI build.mjs exists with --out, --zip, --check, --json, --demo (cli.test.mjs passes); zip writer opens with system unzip (test 41 passes); builder index.html loads (page.test.mjs). Not run: the Chromium-driven builder session README reports for 2026-11-03 (no browser here), so the live preview and download are taken from page.test.mjs only. Roadmap items (form-handling Worker, calendar, multilingual) are honestly listed as not done. README says 39 tests, the suite has 41 (stale count, harmless).
evidence.verification: Ran cd ventures/monastery-site && node --test '*.test.mjs': 41 pass, 0 fail, under 0.5 s. Seeded mutation: changed the custom-accent contrast threshold in checkSite from `r < 4.5` to `r < 3.5` (site.mjs, checkSite accent branch). All 41 tests still passed: the mutation SURVIVED, because the one weak-accent test uses #f5d76e (about 1.4:1) and the strong one #5a1a1a, so no test sits between 3.5 and 4.5. The same boundary check exists for palettes in the contrast test (>= 4.5) so that is covered, but the user-facing checker threshold is not. Reverted by hand; git diff -- ventures/monastery-site is empty. Positive: tests include link/anchor resolution, label and id checks, JSON-LD parsing, hostile input escaping, determinism, demos-equal-engine, zip round trip. Gap: the hostile-input test misses the tab/newline scheme bypass, and no test asserts the sitemap with no site.url.
evidence.craft: Read site.mjs (796 lines: themes, contrast, safeUrl, layout, PAGE builders, orgLd/eventLd/faqLd, normalize, checkSite, parseLines/toLines), build.mjs, usage.mjs, zip.mjs headers. Pure engine with no clock or I/O, esc() applied on output, JSON-LD built as objects, one 65 KB module is large but organised by section, helper names clear. Defects: safeUrl uses /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/ on the raw string, so 'java\tscript:alert(1)' and 'java\nscript:...' are returned unchanged and emitted into href on every page (verified: footer social link and news url) although browsers strip tabs and newlines when parsing URLs; checkSite's link walker uses the same function so it does not warn. Sitemap relative loc with no site.url. Several long template-literal one-liners (site.mjs:401) are hard to review. normalize() silently coerces rather than reporting some bad shapes.
evidence.claims: Checked README claims against files: 'WCAG AA for every pair' backed by site.test.mjs:13 and my recomputation; 'no external scripts, fonts, cookies or analytics, the tests enforce this' backed by page tests (and no external URLs found in built output); 'any link with a scheme the site drops is a high finding' is true for javascript:/data: but FALSE for tab/newline-obfuscated schemes, which the site does not drop and the checklist does not flag; 'hostile input is escaped or dropped' likewise has that hole (self-inflicted: only the community's own config reaches it, so low exploitability); '39 tests' is stale (41); 'a complete static site ... sitemap' holds only when site.url is set, otherwise the sitemap is not valid; 'Driven in Chromium (2026-11-03)' is not backed by a committed artefact I could re-run. Disclaimer present ('Not affiliated with any order, diocese or the Holy See'; no tax claims written by the template, which I confirmed by reading the giving page builder). VENTURE.yaml stage is honestly 'prototype' with hypotheses untested.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a sister who must publish a site: edit examples/abbey.json style config or the builder form, build, get a zip. The engine produces a good-looking, accessible, working site and a launch checklist that asks for the right things (vocation director, https donation page, bequest legal name). Gaps she would hit in the first hour: forms default to mailto: and the roadmap's form handler and one-click deploy are not built, so she must still find a host, upload files by hand and choose a form service; no photo resizing (a 6 MB camera photo goes in the zip as is); English only; sitemap is invalid until she sets the site URL. No real community has used it (usage unmeasured). Works end to end for a technically willing person, not yet 'in an afternoon with no developer' for a typical community.
evidence.domain: Compared against the practice of established monastery sites (Benedictine abbey and convent sites typically list horarium, vocations stages, guesthouse, giving) and WCAG 2.2 contrast (1.4.3, 4.5:1 normal text), schema.org Organization/PlaceOfWorship/Event/FAQPage and the sitemaps.org protocol. Palettes and contrast match WCAG; structured data is valid; vocation page asks for the stages of formation (aspirancy/postulancy, novitiate, temporary and solemn vows) correctly; giving page prints cheque and bequest legal name and never writes tax claims (sound for a US 501(c)(3)-style context, and the checklist tells communities to use their accountant's wording). Departures: no liturgical calendar or Liturgy of the Hours link; no accessibility checks beyond contrast (no axe run, the roadmap lists it); sitemap protocol violation without site.url; no consideration of non-US giving law beyond a free-text statement.

defects.what: safeUrl accepts URLs with an embedded tab or newline in the scheme ('java\tscript:alert(1)'); browsers strip those characters, so it becomes a javascript: URL. It is emitted into href on every page (social, news and other links) and checkSite does not flag it, contradicting the README claim that such links are dropped and flagged. Only reachable from the community's own config, hence medium not high.

With site.url unset, sitemap.xml contains relative <loc>./index.html</loc> entries, invalid under the sitemaps.org protocol; search engines will reject the file. The checklist only reports 'no site URL' as low.
Seeded mutation survived: lowering the checkSite custom-accent contrast threshold from 4.5 to 3.5 passes all 41 tests; no test covers a custom accent between 3.5:1 and 4.5:1.
README says 39 tests; the suite has 41.
The README's Chromium verification (2026-11-03) has no committed artefact to re-run, so it is not independently checkable.

verdict: A tidy, deterministic prototype that does what most of its README says: 41/41 tests pass, I recomputed all 48 palette contrast values in a separate implementation and they match, the giving meter and sitemap with a site URL are right, and the builder never handles money or invents tax claims. It falls short of the bar on verification and claims: a seeded mutation in the custom-accent contrast threshold survived the whole suite, and the README's promise that dangerous link schemes are dropped and flagged is false for tab or newline obfuscated javascript: URLs, which are printed into every page unflagged (self-inflicted by the community's own config, so medium). The sitemap is also invalid unless site.url is set. Fitness is held at 2 because no community can yet receive form submissions without finding their own service, host files by hand, or resize photos; usage is unmeasured. Does not meet the bar (verification 2, claims 2); finished (completeness 3).
